# Seronegative spondyloarthropathies

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Rheumatology and immunology > Joint diseases > Seronegative spondyloarthropathies*

[Original Article Link](/library/J30sjf)

---

## Summary

Seronegative spondyloarthropathies include several chronic inflammatory <u>arthritic</u> diseases that affect the <u>vertebral column</u>. The most important diseases in this group are <u>ankylosing spondylitis</u>, <u>reactive arthritis</u>, and <u>psoriatic arthritis</u>. Common features include the absence of <u>rheumatoid factor</u> (RF) and a strong genetic association with <u>HLA-B27</u>. Spondyloarthropathies disproportionately affect men, with symptom onset generally occurring before the age of 45. The cardinal sign is slowly progressive <u>pain</u> in the lower back and <u>sacroiliac joints</u> (especially at night). Asymmetrical <u>oligoarthritis</u> and <u>enthesopathy</u> are also common. The diseases differ in the involvement of other organs, such as the eyes, the genitourinary tract (particularly in <u>reactive arthritis</u>) or the <u>skin</u> (particularly in <u>psoriatic arthritis</u>). Seronegative spondyloarthropathies usually respond well to <u>NSAID</u> therapy.

## Types of seronegative spondyloarthropathies

The different types of seronegative spondyloarthropathy do not necessarily represent distinct diseases but may overlap significantly in etiology, pathology, clinical features, and treatment.




* <u>Ankylosing spondylitis</u> (most common)

* <u>Reactive arthritis</u>

* <u>Psoriatic arthritis</u>

* Spondyloarthritis associated with <u>inflammatory bowel disease</u> (<u>IBD</u>)

* Undifferentiated spondyloarthropathy

* Peripheral spondyloarthritis

* Non-radiographic <u>axial spondyloarthritis</u>

* Juvenile spondyloarthritis

---

## Common features of seronegative spondyloarthropathies

* Associations [[1]](/library/dXYoCn)

* Negative for <u>rheumatoid factor</u>

* Genetic association with <u>HLA-B27</u>

* <u>Epidemiology</u>

* Generally more commonly affect men

* Age of onset: typically between 20–40 years of age

* Clinical features [[1]](/library/dXYoCn)

* Non-specific symptoms (<u>fever</u>, fatigue, weight loss)

* <u>Arthritis</u>

* Insidious, often unilateral onset

* Particularly of the <u>sacroiliac joints</u> (especially for <u>ankylosing spondylitis</u>)

* Asymmetrical peripheral <u>oligoarthritis</u>

* Stiffness and <u>pain</u> is worse in the morning (typically > 30 minutes) and improves with movement

* Usually responds well to <u>NSAID</u> therapy

* <u>Enthesitis</u> or <u>insertional tendinopathy</u> (e.g., <u>achillodynia</u>)

* <u>Dactylitis</u>: fingers have a sausage-like appearance

* Extra-articular manifestations vary according to type, but involvement of the <u>eye</u> is common (e.g., <u>iritis</u>, <u>iridocyclitis</u>, <u>uveitis</u>)

---

## HLA-B27 associations

* <u>HLA-B27</u> is a surface <u>antigen</u> that belongs to the class I <u>major histocompatibility complex</u> (<u>MHC class I</u>). [[2]](/library/2XYTxn)

* <u>HLA-B27</u> is strongly associated with seronegative spondyloarthropathies and other autoimmune conditions: 

* <u>Ankylosing spondylitis</u>: ∼ 90% [[3]](/library/j5X_PA)

* <u>Psoriatic arthritis</u>: 10–25% [[3]](/library/j5X_PA)[[4]](/library/P5XW4A)

* Acute <u>anterior uveitis</u>: ∼ 50% [[5]](/library/k5Xm4A)[[6]](/library/O5XI4A)

* <u>IBD</u>-associated <u>ankylosing spondylitis</u>: 25–78% [[7]](/library/l5Xv4A)

* <u>Reactive arthritis</u> 50–80% [[8]](/library/45X34A)[[9]](/library/Scaybj)





> [!NOTE]
> A-PAIR of conditions is commonly associated with <u>HLA-B27</u>: Ankylosing <u>spondylitis</u>, Psoriasis, Acute <u>anterior uveitis</u>, Inflammatory bowel disease, Reactive <u>arthritis</u>.
